annotation_description: This is a Dredge deck (Golgari Thug, Narcomoeba, Dread Return, Cabal Therapy, Cephalid Coliseum are all classic Dredge cards). Dredge decks strongly prefer to be on the draw in Legacy because the extra card draw on turn 1 can be replaced with a dredge effect, jumpstarting the entire engine. However, the reasoning given ('drawing an extra card') accidentally arrives at the correct conclusion for the wrong reason. Actually, looking more carefully - the player DID choose to be on the draw, which IS correct for Dredge. The reasoning is slightly wrong (it's not just about drawing an extra card generically, it's specifically about getting a dredge trigger), but the decision itself is correct.

Casting Brainstorm without a fetchland to shuffle away unwanted cards significantly reduces its value. While GPT4om Johnny has a Wasteland (not a fetchland), there's no way to shuffle the library after putting two cards back. Additionally, casting Brainstorm during their own combat phase rather than at end of opponent's turn means they're tapping their only blue mana source during their own turn, losing the ability to hold up Brainstorm as a response to opponent's plays. More importantly, Brainstorm without a shuffle effect is much weaker - it's essentially just card selection rather than card advantage, and the two cards put back will be the next two draws.

Put Force of Will back on top of library with Brainstorm instead of one of the two redundant Murktide Regents. Force of Will is critical interaction that can be cast for free, while the Murktide Regents are extremely expensive with no graveyard fuel to delve. Having two Murktide Regents with only 2 lands and an empty graveyard means at least one is a dead card.

Playing Lion's Eye Diamond before playing a land is slightly suboptimal sequencing. The player should play a land first (Cephalid Coliseum) to maintain maximum options. LED is best deployed right before you need to crack it, and playing it early gives the opponent information. More importantly, the player has Faithless Looting in hand which is a key card to cast - the typical Dredge/reanimator line would be to play a land that produces red (fetch for a red source), cast Faithless Looting, and hold priority to crack LED in response to discard the hand for mana. By playing LED first before fetching, the sequencing still works, but playing the land first would be more standard to ensure you have the right mana base before committing artifacts.

message: Select card to discard (selected 0 of 2, min 2)
annotation_description: Discarding Narcomoeba is suboptimal because Narcomoeba only triggers when milled from library to graveyard, not when already in graveyard. The player's reasoning about dredge synergy is incorrect. Discarding a Cabal Therapy instead would be better since it has flashback from the graveyard (sacrifice a creature), and sacrificing Poxwalkers to flashback Cabal Therapy would trigger Poxwalkers to return to the battlefield, creating a value loop.

Failed to recognize the classic LED + flashback interaction. Could crack LED for RRR (discarding remaining hand), then flashback Faithless Looting for 2R to draw 2 fresh cards. The discarded hand (2x Cephalid Coliseum, 2x Cabal Therapy, Narcomoeba) isn't entirely lost since Cabal Therapy has flashback via creature sacrifice and Narcomoeba can return from graveyard. This would also increase graveyard count toward threshold for Cephalid Coliseum later.

Against what appears to be a combo/graveyard deck with LED in play, drawing Fatal Push before Force of Will may be suboptimal. Force of Will is the premier answer to combo decks and having it in hand immediately gives more protection against a potential combo turn. Fatal Push has limited utility against a deck whose threats come from the graveyard (Poxwalkers, Narcomoeba).

Sonnet ESPN has Cabal Therapy in hand and can cast it for {B} using Lion's Eye Diamond (crack LED for black mana, discarding hand). They also have Poxwalkers in the graveyard which triggers when casting from anywhere other than hand - Faithless Looting flashback from graveyard would return Poxwalkers. Additionally, they could cast Cabal Therapy from hand using Volcanic Island (tapped) or LED for {B}, then flashback the Cabal Therapy from graveyard by sacrificing Narcomoeba (which is in hand but could be cast first for 1U... wait, they only have tapped Volcanic Island). Let me reconsider: They have two LEDs. They could crack one LED for {B} (discarding hand: Cephalid Coliseum, Cabal Therapy, Narcomoeba), then cast Faithless Looting flashback from graveyard for {2}{R} using the other LED cracked for {R} plus... no, that's only 3R and they need 2R. Actually with Volcanic Island tapped they can't use it. But they could cast Cabal Therapy from hand by cracking one LED for BBB (discarding the rest of hand), then use the B to cast Cabal Therapy naming a key card, and Poxwalkers returns from graveyard since... wait, Cabal Therapy is cast from hand, not from 'anywhere other than hand'. But they have 7 cards in graveyard (threshold!), so they could activate Cephalid Coliseum's threshold ability. They passed their entire turn doing nothing when they had available plays like casting Cabal Therapy by cracking LED for black mana.

Drawing Flooded Strand instead of Underground Sea means paying 1 extra life to fetch Underground Sea, when they could have drawn Underground Sea directly and saved the life point. Both lines end up with the same mana, but the opponent has Poxwalkers and aggressive potential, and the player may need to pay 4 life for Snuff Out later, making life points relevant.

Should play the free Lion's Eye Diamond from hand before flashbacking Faithless Looting. LED costs 0 mana and deploying it first maximizes the mana available when cracking LEDs during the flashback. Also should consider playing Cephalid Coliseum as land drop first.

Skipped precombat main phase entirely with multiple productive plays available. Had threshold active on Cephalid Coliseum for draw-3/discard-3, could cast Cabal Therapy to strip opponent's hand, could play Narcomoeba as a body for future Cabal Therapy flashback, could flash back Faithless Looting by cracking LED for red mana, and had a land drop available (second Cephalid Coliseum).

GPT4om Johnny has only 2 lands that produce colored mana (Island + Wasteland producing colorless), but the opponent has Cephalid Coliseums and Volcanic Island as key nonbasic lands. With Sonnet ESPN at 7 cards in graveyard (threshold enabled), the Cephalid Coliseums are very dangerous - they can activate threshold to draw 3/discard 3, enabling graveyard strategies with Poxwalkers and potentially finding combo pieces. Using Wasteland to destroy a Cephalid Coliseum (or Volcanic Island to cut off colored mana) before casting Ponder would be better sequencing. The opponent has 2 LEDs and could potentially combo off. Destroying a Coliseum now is more urgent since threshold is already active. However, casting Ponder first to find a land before potentially needing to sacrifice Wasteland has some merit since GPT4om Johnny needs more mana sources to cast their expensive spells (Murktide, Kaito). Still, the threat of threshold-activated Coliseum is significant enough that Wastelanding first seems correct - and Ponder could then be cast after if they find another land.

message: Select an Island or Swamp card
annotation_description: With Thoughtseize in hand and needing black mana, fetching a basic Swamp instead of Underground Sea is suboptimal. Underground Sea produces both U and B, enabling more flexible mana usage. The player has Wasteland x2 and Island already, so they have no untapped blue sources. Underground Sea would let them cast both Thoughtseize (B) and potentially blue spells. A basic Swamp only produces B, limiting options. While Swamp is immune to Wasteland, the opponent's Wastelands aren't visible and the player's own lands include Wastelands. More importantly, the player needs to eventually cast Kaito (2UB), Murktide Regent (delve but needs UU), and Orcish Bowmasters (1B) - all requiring both colors. With only Island and Swamp as lands, they're very color-constrained compared to having Underground Sea.

Passing on Cephalid Coliseum activation when they have threshold and could fuel their Dredge strategy. The line of sacrificing LED (discarding hand including Golgari Thug to graveyard, generating 3 mana) then activating Coliseum targeting self would allow dredging Golgari Thug (mill 4), drawing 2 more cards, then discarding 3 - massively fueling the graveyard. However, saving for a more set-up turn is defensible.

Against a Dredge deck, Faithless Looting is the primary engine card that enables dredge triggers by replacing draws with dredge and discarding dredge creatures. The opponent already has Cabal Therapy in the graveyard with Poxwalkers to sacrifice for flashback, so they already have access to one Cabal Therapy. Meanwhile, the opponent already has two LEDs on board making the third somewhat redundant.

Activating Cephalid Coliseum before casting Faithless Looting means all 3 draws are normal draws instead of dredges. If they cast Faithless Looting first and discard Golgari Thug to the graveyard, they could then activate Cephalid Coliseum and replace one or more draws with Dredge 4, milling significantly more cards into the graveyard to fuel the dredge strategy.

GPT4om Johnny directed the Orcish Bowmasters ETB trigger at their own Orcish Bowmasters instead of a more useful target. The opponent has Poxwalkers (3/1 with deathtouch) on the battlefield, which is a dangerous creature that could trade up in combat. Dealing 1 damage to Poxwalkers doesn't kill it (it's 3/1), but directing it at the opponent (Sonnet ESPN) would deal 1 damage and still create the Orc Army token. Targeting their own Bowmasters deals 1 damage to their own creature for no benefit whatsoever.

Casting Kaito over Murktide Regent when the graveyard has enough cards to delve out an 8/8 flying Murktide. Against a dredge/reanimator opponent with Ashen Rider in the graveyard, a faster clock is critical. Murktide as an 8/8 flyer represents a 3-turn clock versus Kaito's slower pressure, and both lines leave similar free interaction available (Snuff Out + Force of Will pitching blue).

Not attacking with Kaito alongside the Orc Army Token. Opponent has only one blocker (Poxwalkers with deathtouch). Attacking with both forces the opponent to choose which to block, guaranteeing more damage gets through. Kaito's 0 ability draws cards when the opponent lost life this turn, making connecting with Kaito especially valuable.

Sonnet ESPN had threshold active on Cephalid Coliseum (12 cards in graveyard) and could have activated it targeting themselves to dredge with Golgari Thug. They also had Cabal Therapy in graveyard that could be flashed back by sacrificing Poxwalkers, which would trigger Bridge from Below (in hand, but could be discarded via Coliseum/LED). Instead they just played a free LED and passed the turn, missing significant dredge engine advancement.

Sonnet ESPN incorrectly believed it was the opponent's turn when it was actually their own Turn 8 precombat main phase. They passed without using any abilities, wasting critical progression for their Dredge strategy. They have threshold on Cephalid Coliseum (draw 3/discard 3), flashback Otherworldly Gaze available, and need to get Golgari Thug and Bridge from Below into the graveyard to enable their dredge engine.

Poxwalkers is a 3/1 with deathtouch - dealing 1 damage kills it. While it can return from the graveyard when Sonnet ESPN casts spells from non-hand zones, removing a deathtouch creature even temporarily is much more valuable than 1 face damage when the opponent is at 15 life. The deathtouch creature threatens to trade with Kaito or any other attacker.

Blocked Poxwalkers (3/1 deathtouch, recursive) with Orcish Bowmasters, trading a high-value permanent to save only 3 life. Poxwalkers will return whenever Sonnet casts spells from graveyard (they have multiple flashback cards available). Bowmasters provides ongoing value by punishing card draws and growing the Orc Army token.

Casting Murktide Regent before using Wasteland on Cephalid Coliseum. The opponent is a Dredge deck at threshold with Cephalid Coliseum active, which could enable powerful dredge turns. Wasting a Coliseum first removes a key enabler and costs nothing since Murktide uses Delve, not lands for mana beyond UU.

Opponent is at 8 life with a dredge deck that can explode at any time. Attacking with only 1 creature instead of both leaves significant damage on the table. Golgari Thug (1/1) can only block one attacker, so the other gets through for full damage. With both attackers, you'd deal significantly more damage and put the opponent in lethal range much sooner.

At 8 life facing lethal pressure, Sonnet ESPN declined to activate Cephalid Coliseum's threshold ability during combat. With 14 cards in graveyard (threshold active), they could tap one Coliseum for U (taking 1 damage) and sacrifice the other to draw 3/discard 3, potentially dredging Golgari Thug (mill 4 per dredge replacement) and discarding Bridge from Below to the graveyard where it generates zombies. This would massively advance their graveyard combo at the cost of just 1 life.

At 3 life with the opponent's 2/2 attacking (going to 1 life), Sonnet ESPN passed priority without using Lion's Eye Diamond to discard their hand (Bridge from Below, Poxwalkers, Stinkweed Imp) to the graveyard. Getting Bridge from Below into the graveyard is critical for the dredge strategy - it creates zombie tokens when nontoken creatures die. Stinkweed Imp provides dredge 5. They could have also used the LED mana + Volcanic Island to flashback Otherworldly Gaze for surveil 3, setting up dredges for their next turn.
